g.text: WSL 2: one lightweight VM, one Linux kernel, several isolated distributions
What this guide relies on: a normal Ubuntu distribution with its own Docker Engine and Tailscale.
Hyper-V hypervisor (Windows itself runs on top of it)
WSL 2 utility VM (one Microsoft-built Linux kernel, shared)
Docker Desktop's Engine (managed by Docker Desktop)
Docker docs: isolated from other distros the way any two
distros are; interacts only if WSL integration is enabled.
Networking (Microsoft docs): the default mode is NAT: the VM has its own virtual adapter and IP behind Windows (so Tailscale in WSL is behind that NAT too). "mirrored"
mode shares the host's interfaces; "bridged" is deprecated since WSL 2.4.5.
Docker's WSL docs warn that running Docker Desktop and a separate Engine inside WSL can conflict: disable Desktop's WSL integration for this distro.
